seed.title: MITCHELL-RILEY SYNDROME
alt_titles: DIABETES, NEONATAL, WITH PANCREATIC HYPOPLASIA, INTESTINAL ATRESIA, AND GALLBLADDER APLASIA OR HYPOPLASIA

HP:0001522.label: Death in infancy
HP:0001522.text: death in first year of life

HP:0006476.label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells
HP:0006476.text: absence of insulin, glucagon and somatostatin staining in pancreatic islets

records.label: 2 sibs
quotes: We studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern which includes low birthweight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias.
This constellation of congenital anomalies appears to be a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome.

records.label: 3 unrelated infants from ECEMC
quotes: A computerized search of the data files of the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC) identified 3 other unrelated infants with intestinal atresias, hypospadias, and low birth weight. These cases may represent a milder expression of the same syndrome.

records.label: Patients with lethal autosomal recessive IUGR, biliary atresia and esophageal/duodenal atresia syndrome
quotes: Lethal autosomal recessive syndrome with intrauterine growth retardation, intra- and extrahepatic biliary atresia, and esophageal and duodenal atresia.

records.label: Five infants (two sibling pairs and an isolated case)

phenotypes.text: death in first year of life
absence of insulin, glucagon and somatostatin staining in pancreatic islets
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells

quotes: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia. One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents.
One patient with a milder form is surviving free of insulin. Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management.
Pancreatic immunohistochemistry revealed few scattered chromogranin-A-positive cell clusters but complete absence of insulin, glucagon and somatostatin.

records.label: Patient (female infant)
quotes: We describe a patient born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern characterized by low birth weight, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and intestinal malrotation. The infant died 60 days after birth.
Chromosomes at 550-600 band levels were normal for a female (46,XX).

records.label: Patient born to consanguineous parents
quotes: We report a patient born to consanguineous parents as a further example of a recently described phenotype comprising neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias and gall bladder agenesis.
Our case is the first to have neonatal diabetes without a demonstrable structural pancreatic abnormality, showing that a deficit in pancreatic function is involved.

records.label: Newborn from consanguineous parents
quotes: We report on a newborn from consanguineous parents who presented with multiple congenital anomalies and neonatal hemochromatosis.

The syndrome consisted of intra-uterine growth retardation, intestinal atresia, gallbladder aplasia and diabetes mellitus, and fitted with the diagnosis of Martinez-Frias syndrome, a very rare autosomal recessive phenotype

records.label: Proband #1
records.age_last: died in the first few months of life

phenotypes.text: absence of insulin-, glucagon- and somatostatin-staining pancreatic cells at autopsy
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells

records.segregation: inherited from carrier parents; homozygosity region excluded overlap with unaffected sib
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q

autopsies of two cases (proband #1 and case 3 in Ref) revealed normal-appearing exocrine pancreata with clusters of ChromograninA-positive cells but total absence of cells staining for insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin

The disease locus was mapped using overlapping homozygosity in probands #1and #2 (see Supplementary material for pedigree information and references to previous clinical case reports) respectively the offspring of first and second cousins.

records.label: Proband #2
records.segregation: inherited from carrier parents (offspring of second cousins)
quotes: Proband #2, still alive at age 4.5 years, had the homozygous missense mutation 217 Ser>Pro, confirming the unbiased exon sequencing described above. All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.

records.label: Proband #3
quotes: Proband #3, still alive at the age of 9 and intermittently off insulin, was a compound heterozygote for donor-site loss in intron 6 (IVS6+2 t>g) and disruption of the acceptor site in intron 1 (IVS1-12 a>g).

records.label: Proband #4
records.age_last: died in the first few months of life
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q

records.label: Proband #5
records.age_last: died in the first few months of life
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q involving a highly conserved arginine in the DNA-binding domain

records.label: Proband #6
records.segregation: no RFX6 or NEUROG3 point mutation or RFX6 deletion in parents; proband DNA unavailable
quotes: Finally, we failed to identify any mutation in RFX6 in proband #6. In the absence of DNA from the proband, we sequenced both parents and found no point mutation of RFX6 or NEUROG3; and long-range PCR did not reveal any deletions of RFX6
In the absence of proband DNA we cannot rule out a de novo mutation, but this case is most likely a phenocopy.

records.label: Case 1 (I5)
records.onset: diabetes at 3 years; intestinal atresia at birth
records.segregation: Father heterozygous for p.Arg726X, mother heterozygous for p.Arg866X; inherited from both grandmothers
quotes: Case 1 (Figure 1, I5), current age 9 years, is a female born at 32 weeks' gestation, birth weight 1.65 kg (42nd centile), with duodenal atresia, jejunal web and Meckel's diverticulum.
She presented at the age of 3 years with diabetic ketoacidosis.

Genetic testing showed that both children are compound heterozygotes for the RFX6 nonsense mutations c.2176C>T (p.Arg726X) and c.2596C>T (p.Arg866X) in exons 17 and 18, respectively (Figure 2). The fathers were heterozygous for p.Arg726X and the mothers heterozygous for p.Arg866X.

records.label: Case 2 (I12)
records.onset: diabetes at 6 years; intestinal atresia at birth
records.segregation: Father heterozygous for p.Arg726X, mother heterozygous for p.Arg866X; inherited from both grandmothers
quotes: Case 2 (Figure 1, I12), her double first cousin, current age 9 years, is a male infant who was born at 34 weeks gestation, birth weight 1.70 kg (7th centile), with duodenal atresia and mid-gut malrotation. He was diagnosed with diabetes having presented with hyperglycemia (16.0 mmol/l) at the age of 6 years.
His past history is notable for chronic iron deficiency anemia.
No structural abnormality of the hepato-biliary tract has been identified, and his liver function tests have always been within normal limits.

notes.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) noted that the RFX6 R866X mutation in exon 18 lies within 50 nucleotides of the last exon-exon boundary and is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay, producing a truncated protein that keeps the full DNA-binding domain and possibly some function, whereas R726X is predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay. They suggested this partial retention of function might explain the milder phenotype and later onset of diabetes.
quotes: The exon 18 mutation, c.2596C>T (R866X) is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay because it lies within 50 nucleotides of the last exon–exon boundary of the gene.

It is possible that escape from NMD could lead to some retention of function of the RFX6 protein generated from that allele, with a resulting milder phenotype with respect to age of onset of diabetes and other clinical features.

notes.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) reviewed 8 previously reported molecularly confirmed cases of Mitchell-Riley syndrome. In those cases, the mutations either disrupted splicing or the reading frame in exons 2-8 or were missense changes clustered at the DNA-binding domain, and diabetes started within the first 2 weeks of life. By contrast, their 2 patients had 3-prime truncating mutations, diabetes starting in childhood, no liver disease, and longer survival.
quotes: Among the nine mutations identified in these eight cases (one a compound heterozygote, the remaining seven homozygous), six affect splicing and/or the reading frame in exons 2–8; the remaining three are mis-sense mutations clustering within or close to the DNA-binding domain (Figure 2).

Aside from the difference in age of onset of diabetes in the two new cases, the phenotype differed from previously published cases in the absence of any liver pathology, although one of the cases (case 1) had absent gall bladder.

notes.statement: In their review of 8 previously reported cases, Sansbury et al. (2015) found duodenal atresia in all cases, gallbladder agenesis in 7 of 8, and intrahepatic cholestasis in 7 of 8. Five of the 8 children had died, all within the first year of life.
quotes: Duodenal atresia is a present in all cases, with or without jejunal atresia/mid-gut malrotation. Gall-bladder agenesis is present in 7/8. All cases had evidence of liver involvement with intrahepatic cholestasis in 7/8 cases and ascites in a further case. Five of the eight children had died, all within the first year of life.

notes.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) found that heterozygous carriers of the RFX6 mutations in their family, including several relatives with adult-onset diabetes, had no difference in C-peptide or HbA1c levels compared with noncarriers. They concluded that the data did not support heterozygosity as a risk factor for diabetes.
quotes: Taking these data together, there is no support for the idea that being heterozygous for either RFX6 mutation is a risk factor for abnormal HbA1c or C-peptide levels, or diabetes.

notes.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) recommended considering RFX6 genetic testing in patients with intestinal atresias even when neonatal diabetes is absent, especially when autosomal recessive inheritance is suspected.
quotes: Genetic testing for RFX6 mutations should be considered in patients presenting with intestinal atresias in the absence of neonatal diabetes, especially where sibling recurrence or parental consanguinity point to possible autosomal recessive inheritance.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) described human infants with neonatal diabetes and small bowel obstruction due to bowel atresia, with some reduction in pancreatic size but no exocrine enzyme deficiency, hypoplastic gallbladder, and intractable diarrhea unresponsive to pancreatic enzyme replacement. Autopsies showed normal-appearing exocrine pancreas with chromogranin A-positive cell clusters but no cells staining for insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin.
quotes: The phenotype of the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice is remarkably similar to human patients born with neonatal diabetes and small bowel obstruction due to bowel atresia. Despite some reduction in pancreatic size, these cases were not deficient in enzymes of the exocrine pancreas
In addition, the syndrome involves hypoplastic gall bladder, and intractable diarrhea unresponsive to pancreatic enzyme replacement.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) proposed the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome, after the two clinicians who first described it, distinguishing it from Martinez-Frias syndrome, whose original patients had esophageal atresia and hypospadias without diabetes and in one of whom no RFX6 mutation was found.
quotes: However, since the original MFS patients also had oesophageal atresia and hypospadias, and did not have diabetes, and we did not find any RFX6 mutation in the parents of one case of MFS, our cases are distinct from MFS. We propose to name their condition, now of defined molecular aetiology, the Mitchell-Riley syndrome

notes.statement: By homozygosity mapping in 2 consanguineous probands, Smith et al. (2010) identified 3 shared regions of homozygosity totaling 24 Mb (2p15-16, 6q21-22, 6q23); of 194 genes in these regions, only RFX6, in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas-enriched expression.
quotes: Only three HBD regions were common in the two probands, totaling 24 Mb (Table 1). Altogether, 194 RefSeq genes map to these regions. Of these genes, only RFX6, which falls in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas–enriched expression in the TiGER database

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) used targeted capture and deep sequencing of exons in the shared homozygous regions in proband 2 and found only one nonsynonymous novel variant, S217P in RFX6; direct sequencing of RFX6 identified mutations in 5 of 6 probands, with homozygous severe mutations associated with death in early infancy and milder genotypes with survival.
quotes: The only non-synonymous variant was 217 Ser>Pro in RFX6, identifying this gene as the most likely candidate.
Missense, splicing or frameshift mutations in RFX6 were found in five of the six available probands (Fig. 5e) with an interesting genotype-phenotype correlation.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found that the R181Q mutation, in the DNA-binding domain, completely abrogated DNA binding, whereas S217P only modestly reduced DNA binding and did not affect dimer formation. Properly spliced RFX6 transcript was not detected in autopsy pancreas from the proband homozygous for the intron 2 splice donor mutation.
quotes: We found that 181R>Q (proband #5), which alters a conserved amino acid in the DNA binding domain, completely abrogated DNA binding, while 217S>P (proband #2), which lies between the DNA-binding domain and dimerization domain of Rfx6, only modestly reduced DNA binding (Fig. 5d) and did not affect dimer formation
we amplified RFX6 mRNA by RT-PCR of high-quality RNA from autopsy pancreas and failed to detect the properly spliced transcript

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice were born at Mendelian ratios but failed to feed, had gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction, and died within 2 days of birth; some had reduced pancreas size. Their pancreata contained many endocrine cells but none expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin, or ghrelin, while pancreatic polypeptide-expressing cells were increased.
quotes: homozygous Rfx6eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio, but failed to feed normally, exhibited gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction (Fig. 3e-f) and died within 2 days post partum.
the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre pancreata still contained a large number of endocrine cells, but confirmed that none of these cells expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin or ghrelin

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) showed that Rfx6 is expressed broadly in definitive endoderm, becomes restricted to gut and pancreatic bud, and is reactivated downstream of Neurogenin3 in islet progenitors, being absent from Neurog3-null pancreas. Rfx6 formed a heterodimeric DNA-binding complex with Rfx3 on an X-box site and cooperated in activating an X-box promoter; Rfx6 loss did not affect primary cilia formation.
quotes: Rfx6 is expressed initially broadly in the definitive endoderm after gastrulation, becomes restricted to the gut and pancreatic bud at mid gestation, is reactivated by Neurogenin3 in islet progenitor cells and is ultimately restricted to pancreatic islets in the mature pancreas.

We found that both full length Rfx3, and truncations that retain the DNA-binding and dimerization domains, bound to an X box site together with Rfx6 (Fig. 5a and Supplemenatry Fig. S10), and that the two factors cooperated in activating a promoter containing multimers of this X box site

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found no common variants in the RFX6 linkage disequilibrium block associated with type 1 or type 2 diabetes in genomewide association data.
quotes: a search of the RFX6 linkage disequilibrium block in our genome-wide association data, combined with those of the WTCC, did not reveal any common variants associated with type 1 or type 2 diabetes

notes.statement: Martinovici et al. (2010) suggested that neonatal hemochromatosis may be part of the Martinez-Frias syndrome, having observed it in a consanguineous newborn with intestinal atresia, gallbladder aplasia, and diabetes mellitus.
quotes: We suggest that neonatal hemochromatosis may be part of the Martinez-Frias syndrome.

notes.statement: Chappell et al. (2008) considered it likely that the syndrome of neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias and gallbladder agenesis is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: It is likely that this disorder is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

notes.statement: In their patient, Chappell et al. (2008) found no mutations in genes with a recognized role in monogenic diabetes, including KCNJ11, ABCC8, GCK, IPF1, HNF1B, NEUROD1 and TCF7L2, or in the candidate gene HNF6, which is involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic development.
quotes: We sequenced genes with a recognized role in monogenic forms of diabetes, including KCNJ11, ABCC8, GCK, IPF1, HNF1beta, NeuroD1 and TCF7L2, as well as a novel candidate gene, HNF6, known to be involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic development, but did not identify mutations.

notes.statement: Chappell et al. (2008) proposed that previously reported cases with overlapping features, including malrotation, biliary atresia and pancreatic hypoplasia (e.g., those described by Martinez-Frias), may represent variations of the same syndrome.
quotes: Other reports have described cases with overlapping patterns including malrotation, biliary atresia and pancreatic hypoplasia (e.g. as described by Martínez-Frías). We propose that these cases may represent variations of the same syndrome.

notes.statement: Galán-Gómez et al. (2007) concluded that their patient, born to consanguineous parents, confirmed the autosomal recessive disorder (Martínez-Frías syndrome) previously described by their group.
quotes: This patient confirmed the autosomal recessive disorder previously described by our group.

notes.statement: Galán-Gómez et al. (2007) suggested that the pathogenesis of the syndrome is most probably of blastogenetic origin, mainly affecting the midline developmental duodenal-biliary-pancreatic junction.
quotes: The pathogenesis of this syndrome is most probably of blastogenetic origin mainly affecting midline developmental duodenal biliary pancreatic junction.

notes.statement: In one affected infant from the consanguineous family, Mitchell et al. (2004) found no duplication or uniparental isodisomy of PLAGL1 at 6q24, no contiguous gene deletion involving the glucokinase gene, and no mutation in the coding sequences or splice sites of PDX1.
quotes: In one case from the consanguineous family, molecular analysis showed no duplication or uniparental isodisomy of PLAGL-1 at 6q24, no contiguous gene deletion involving the glucokinase gene, and no mutation in the coding sequences or splice sites of PDX-1.

notes.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) concluded that the combination of neonatal diabetes, pancreatic hypoplasia, intestinal atresia and gallbladder hypoplasia probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome, based on affected sib pairs including one born to consanguineous parents.
quotes: This combination of multiple congenital abnormalities has not been previously described and probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome involving a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development and whose aetiology is as yet unknown.

notes.statement: Gentile and Fiorente (1999) reported esophageal, duodenal, rectoanal and biliary atresia, intestinal malrotation, malformed/hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias, and presented this as further evidence of a new distinct syndrome.
quotes: Esophageal, duodenal, rectoanal and biliary atresia, intestinal malrotation, malformed/hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias: further evidence of a new distinct syndrome.

notes.statement: Annerén et al. (1998) described a lethal syndrome of intrauterine growth retardation, intra- and extrahepatic biliary atresia, and esophageal and duodenal atresia, which they considered to be autosomal recessive.
quotes: Lethal autosomal recessive syndrome with intrauterine growth retardation, intra- and extrahepatic biliary atresia, and esophageal and duodenal atresia.

notes.statement: Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) suggested autosomal recessive inheritance of a syndrome of low birthweight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias, based on its occurrence in 2 sibs born to consanguineous parents.
quotes: We studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern
This constellation of congenital anomalies appears to be a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome.
